candidate_077.name: correlation-admissible multi-instrument evidence sharing with objective-separated acquisition
candidate_077.mechanism_hypothesis: When multiple scientific instruments observe different but physically related outputs, keep each instrument's acquisition objective separate while sharing only empirically supported cross-output information through a joint probabilistic model. Schedule heterogeneous instruments using their actual measurement costs/latencies, and suppress or shrink cross-output transfer when correlation support is weak so that one channel cannot contaminate another through negative transfer.

primary_evidence.source: Chih-Yu Lee et al., Real-time Multi-instrument Autonomous Discovery of Novel Phase-change Memory Materials, arXiv:2605.18033, 2026-05-18.
primary_evidence.physical_loop: The MAD system couples XRD structural mapping and electrical-resistance optimization in one closed loop. A single XRD scan is about 15 minutes while an electrical measurement is about 1.5 minutes, so the instruments have strongly asymmetric costs. Structural mapping uses maximum uncertainty while resistance optimization uses expected improvement; a multi-output coregionalized GP shares posterior information between the seven NMF structural components and resistance rather than collapsing both tasks into one scalar objective.
primary_evidence.system_result: On Mn-Sb-Te combinatorial libraries the system completed 25 closed-loop iterations in about 5 hours and reports roughly a seven-fold speed-up relative to traditional grid mapping, while identifying high-resistance and high-resistance-contrast compositions.
primary_evidence.component_like_benchmark: The paper also reports in-silico comparisons against independent GPs and random sampling. The coregionalized strategy reaches 95% structural similarity with fewer samples than independent models, while optimization regret approaches zero faster and more stably. This supports cross-instrument knowledge sharing when the outputs are genuinely correlated, while retaining distinct acquisition objectives.
primary_evidence.boundary_evidence: Multi-output GP literature establishes a failure boundary: when outputs do not actually share common structure, joint models can suffer negative transfer and perform worse than independent or subset models. Therefore cross-instrument sharing should be treated as an admissible, revisable relation rather than an always-on assumption.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This adds a missing layer to candidates_071/072/076: separate discovery/coverage or fidelity lanes can still exchange evidence when a tested physical relation exists, without merging their objectives. A higher-level scientist controller should decide not only which lane or fidelity to query, but also which other measurement channels are allowed to update that lane's posterior.
primary_evidence.limits: The physical demonstration is one material system and the reported seven-fold acceleration is versus grid mapping, not an isolated ablation of every orchestration component. The in-silico independent-GP comparison is stronger for the value of data fusion but remains model-based. The paper does not provide a dynamic correlation-admissibility gate, so the negative-transfer safeguard is a synthesis with established multi-output-GP failure theory rather than a directly tested MAD component.
